title: Ask, Answer, Explain
objectives: I can ask a question and give an answer.
I can describe something so a friend can picture it.
I can explain how or why in my own words.
I can share an idea and remember what I learned.
rationale: These six words are the language of every first-grade lesson: asking, answering, describing, explaining, sharing ideas, and remembering. They open the year so later directions such as 'describe the picture' or 'explain your thinking' are understood the first time. Describe and explain are used all year, and children revisit the kindergarten words listen, share, and different here, so the unit connects to what they already know.

words.def: Something you ask to find out more.
words.ex: Mia raised her hand to ask a question about the story.
words.ex2: At dinner, Dad asked me a question about my day.
words.nonExample: "My dog is brown" is not a question because it tells something.

apps.academic: Raise your hand when you have a question.
apps.writing: End a sentence with a question mark when it asks something.

cloze.s: Max did not know how bees make honey, so he asked a ___.

cloze2.s: Who made this? What is it for? Zoe had many ___ about the new toy.

misuse.s: "The sky is blue," said Leo, and that is a good question.
misuse.why: "The sky is blue" tells something. It does not ask anything.

visual.alt: A child raising a hand beside a big question mark.

words.def: What you say or write when someone asks.
words.ex: Kofi knew the answer and said it out loud.
words.ex2: The answer to two plus two is four.
words.nonExample: "What is your name?" is a question, not an answer.

apps.academic: Write your answer in a whole sentence.
apps.spoken: I think the answer is yes.
apps.writing: Start with the question's words when you write your answer.

cloze.s: The teacher asked, "What is two plus two?" Ben's ___ was four.

cloze2.s: I did not know the ___, so I looked in a book.

misuse.s: Dad asked me what I wanted for lunch. I said, "What is for lunch?" and that was my answer.
misuse.why: That asks another question. It does not tell Dad what you want.

visual.alt: A speech bubble next to a green check mark.

words.def: Tell what something looks, sounds, or feels like.
words.ex: Can you describe your pet to the class?
words.ex2: He used soft words to describe the sleepy kitten.
words.nonExample: Saying only the word "dog" does not describe the dog.

apps.academic: Describe the picture with three words.
apps.spoken: Let me describe my lunch box.
apps.writing: Use colors, sizes, and shapes to describe what you see.

cloze.s: Please ___ the picture. Tell us the colors and shapes you see.

cloze2.s: To ___ the soup, Lin said it was hot, salty, and thick.

misuse.s: Pia described her dog by saying only the word "dog."
misuse.why: To describe means to tell what something is like. A name alone gives no details.

visual.alt: A magnifying glass over a colorful crayon drawing.

words.def: Tell how or why so others can understand.
words.ex: Dad will explain how the toy car works.
words.ex2: The bus driver stopped to explain why we were late.
words.nonExample: Just saying "It works!" does not explain how.

apps.academic: Explain your thinking to your partner.
apps.spoken: Let me explain what I mean.
apps.writing: Write one reason to explain your answer.

cloze.s: Ravi did not know how to play, so Mom will ___ the rules.

cloze2.s: Can you ___ why the plant is dry? Tell us what happened to it.

misuse.s: To explain how to brush teeth, Jo walked out of the room without saying a word.
misuse.why: To explain means to tell how or why with words. Leaving without speaking explains nothing.

visual.alt: A child talking with a light bulb above their head.

words.def: A thought you have in your mind.
words.ex: I have an idea for a fun game.
words.ex2: Jo's idea was to build a fort from boxes.
words.nonExample: You cannot hold an idea in your hand like a rock.

apps.academic: Share your idea with a partner.
apps.writing: Write your best idea and one reason it is good.

cloze.s: Zara had a great ___: she would make a card for Grandma.

cloze2.s: We could not agree on a game until Tom shared his ___.

misuse.s: I put my idea in my backpack so it would not get wet.
misuse.why: An idea is a thought in your mind. You cannot put it in a bag.

visual.alt: A glowing light bulb above a brain.

words.def: Think of something you learned or saw before.
words.ex: I remember my first day of school.
words.ex2: Please remember your coat when you go outside.
words.nonExample: If I leave my hat at school, I did not remember it.

apps.academic: Remember to put your name on your paper.
apps.writing: Write about something you remember from last summer.

cloze.s: Please ___ to bring your library book on Friday so you can pick a new one.

cloze2.s: Lila could ___ her grandma's house, even the blue door, from last summer.

misuse.s: I remember the party that I will go to next year.
misuse.why: Remember is about what already happened or what you learned. Next year has not come yet.

visual.alt: A brain next to a calendar page.

passage.title: Show and Tell
paras: Sam brought a shell to show and tell. Mia had a question: "Can you describe it?" Sam gave his answer: "It is small, pink, and bumpy." Then Mia asked him to explain where he found it. "I remember the beach," said Sam. "It was Dad's idea to look under the rocks."

qs.q: Mia asks Sam to describe the shell. What does she want him to do?
choices: Tell what the shell looks like.
qs.why: To describe is to tell what something looks like, and Sam says it is small, pink, and bumpy.

qs.q: Where did Sam find the shell?
qs.why: Sam remembers the beach when he explains where he found it.

qs.q: What is this story mostly about?
qs.why: Mia asks questions and Sam tells about the shell he brought.

write.prompt: Draw something you could bring for show and tell. Then say or write a sentence that describes it.

study.task: Clap the beats in each word. Which two words have three beats?

sentences: Say or write a question to ask a friend.
Use the word describe to tell about your favorite toy.
Say a sentence with the word idea about something to do at recess.

combine.model: Mia asked a question, and Sam gave an answer.
I remember the red bird I saw.

discuss: What is a good question to ask on the first day of school?
How do you remember things like your lunch or your coat?
produce.explain: Explain how to do something you are good at, like tying a shoe or drawing a cat.

constructed.prompt: Say or write one question about a pet. Then give an answer to your own question.
look: gives an answer that fits the question
constructed.model: My question is, "What does a fish eat?" The answer is, "A fish eats fish food."

constructed.prompt: Pick a toy. Describe it. Then explain how you play with it.
look: tells how or why in order
constructed.model: I describe my ball: it is round, red, and bouncy. I explain how I play: I throw it to my friend and she throws it back.

teacher.overview: Children learn six words they hear in every lesson and use them to ask, answer, describe, explain, and share thinking. The unit also revisits the kindergarten words listen, share, and different.

notes.va.question.n: Hold up a picture and let children ask questions about it. Point out that a question asks and a statement tells; the mark at the end is a clue.
notes.va.answer.n: Pair with question every time. Have one child ask and another answer in a whole sentence, so answer is more than one word.
notes.va.describe.v: Use a mystery object in a bag. Children describe it with their senses without naming it. Models: 'It is soft. It is round.'
notes.va.explain.v: Explain adds a how or why. Compare 'I like it' with 'I like it because it is soft.' Keep the because for the next unit.
notes.va.idea.n: An idea is in your mind, not an object. Draw a thought bubble. Ask for a different idea after each child shares.
notes.va.remember.v: Show a picture for ten seconds, then hide it and ask what children remember. Link to forget as the opposite.

teacher.model: Think-aloud: 'Sam has a shell. I have a question, so I ask, "What color is it?" He gives an answer, so I know it is pink. Now I can describe it to you: small, pink, and bumpy. I can even explain where he found it, because I remember the beach.'
discuss: What question would you ask a new friend?
Tell about something you remember from yesterday.
misconceptions: Answer means only the right answer; any reply to a question is an answer.
Explain means to say it louder or again.
An idea has to be written down to count.
extend: Children make a question jar: each writes or draws one question and a partner draws an answer.
Play 'I describe, you draw': one child describes, the partner draws what they hear.
teacher.reviewAdvice: Revisit describe and explain the next day with a new picture, again at one week, and use them whenever children share work. Both return in later units.

wida.oral: Partner A describes one classroom object without naming it. Partner B asks one question, then gives an answer with the name of the object.

needsReview: Spanish glosses (pregunta, respuesta, describir, explicar, idea, recordar) are not reviewed by a native speaker.
The describe ladder (say, tell, describe, explain) is a rough sequence of how much detail, not a strict scale.
